caveat: Framework only: never taught, piloted or evaluated, and the 'epistemic agent' claim is asserted without engaging philosophy of technology.
title: Conceptualising student-GenAI knowledge co-creation in higher education
venue: Innovations in Education and Teaching International
why: Proposes a four-stage pedagogy (exploration, epistemic friction, simulation, circulation) treating GenAI as a co-creator and 'active epistemic agent'. Strip the model out and stages 1, 2 and 4 are inquiry, source criticism and knowledge circulation — a useful foil for Professional Criticality.
abstract: The conceptual paper aims to propose a framework to support students in critically engaging with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a co-creative partner in knowledge generation. Grounded on the connectivism theory, a four-stage pedagogical framework of student-GenAI knowledge co-creation, composed of Generative Exploration (stage 1), Epistemic Friction (stage 2), Experiential Stimulation (stage 3), and Knowledge Circulation (stage 4), is proposed. Research avenues, including engagement, critical thinking, trust & scepticism, professional competence development, and epistemic ownership, for future inquiries are also mapped out, structured around the four stages.
